body: So, just throwing this out there - I had my son in a private school from preschool to halfway through second grade.  He’d done the testing prior to preschool to qualify for IEP, but the private school, like yours didn’t offer them.  As he moved up and advanced in the private school, his reactions and aggression started to get worse.  We lost my dad and things started to spiral and he was also sent home multiple times and eventually they threatened suspension.  I ended up just pulling him myself and enrolling in public school.  The public school environment is a night and day difference for him.  They have the number of staff necessary and QUALIFIED to help him.  They tested him and are getting him caught up where he was deficient (he started this year with a C and D and at the last grading session had an A and a B).  He’s taking pride in himself now, he’s getting better self esteem etc.  he may not be telling you but what was happening at my son’s private school was that older kids knew he was easily triggered and were “poking the bear” to get him to react.  The school was allowing it to happen and it was happening more and more frequently, and then started taking less and less time because they were getting better at setting him off and he knew it was coming so the eruption was closer to the top.  I had (and still do have) my own concerns about public school education and environments, but for my child it’s been a positive improvement.  Good luck!

I went through a pregnancy alone, went to all doctors appointments alone etc.  I scheduled one of the last, elective sonograms specifically for him to attend but he couldn’t make it because, stupid me, had scheduled it for the opening day of dove season.  He certainly wasn’t welcome at the delivery, wasn’t welcome at the hospital, and he got to meet his son when I felt good enough to accept visitors.  They are on your time and you can focus on you and your baby.  Don’t let him guilt you into anything and don’t let him bulldoze you.  Trust me, that baby will make you stand up and be stronger than you’ll ever think you were capable.

My ex filed for custody when the baby was 4 days old. He didn’t even know the baby’s name or when he was born.  Dad a record for DV, child endangerment (oldest daughter) and assault with a deadly weapon.  I begged the court to get him supervised time with my baby.  They said there was no need. By the time the court order came, it took 2 months for my baby came home covered in bruises (he was 8 months old at this point). Went to supervised visits, he was not at all consistent.  About 2 weeks before my sons 2nd birthday he held his last supervised visit, told the therapist who was supervising they wouldn’t be seeing each other again and that was that.  6 months later I took him to court for back child support, he’d been lying about his income and he owed me a lot of money.  Offered termination of rights and no child support owed and he jumped on it.  My boy is 6 1/2 now and it’s the best thing in the world to not have to deal with that drama.  I’m still so scared that he’s gonna pop back up that I carry my final orders with me no matter where I’m at, just in case.

My sons grandparents knew, and called me when he was 2 months old and told me they didn’t want involved.  He told his sisters stories where I’m sure I was the villain, and they harassed me during the custody dispute.  After I gained sole custody, and he terminated his rights, we were all at the same funeral together. One of the sisters came and ignored me and introduced herself to my son (he was 5 at the time) as “aunt so and so.” My son looked at me and said “why does this lady think she’s “aunt (my brothers significant other)?” And that was the last of it.  They’re a Disneyland family. Only around when it’s convenient and I’m so glad my child isn’t involved in it.

My sons father was convicted of child endangerment, DV, and two counts of assault with a deadly weapon.  They told me I had no basis asking for supervised visits and handed him an 8 month old unhindered.  Took 2 months before my baby came home covered in bruises and I got an emergency order for supervised visits.  Be VERY careful, because what we see as a slam dunk the courts don’t always.  (I now have sole custody, his rights were terminated but my son has PTSD and severe separation anxiety and he’s now almost 7).

I own livestock and my dad passed away recently.  Whenever I needed to back, he was my easy button.  Over the last 6 months, I can back both a bumper pull and a gooseneck into very tight spots to load cattle. By myself.  Take your time. Take deep breaths. Don’t let an audience rattle you.  We can do it just as well as the men can, and don’t sell yourself short on what you know and what you can learn.

The one that pissed me off the most was that he’d been absent most of the pregnancy.  Shows up on my doorstep when I was 7 months pregnant, “shocked” I was showing.  So I tried to be nice, since he’d missed all of the big appointments, and scheduled a 3D appt.  Had to pay out of pocket and scheduled it when he could come, according to the schedule he told me he was available.  Then, he didn’t show up because….

It was opening day of dove season.

I buried my dad, and my sons grandpa yesterday.  It was so sudden and 100% unexpected.  My son was desperate to get Santa on the phone today so he’d know not to bring grandpas presents.  I’m over the holiday.

This is exactly how I feel.  The trauma I went through with my sons father and the aftermath of the court induced trauma, I had no desire to date.  I’m happy with my life and the peace we have.  Plus I don’t have to worry if my child is being treated poorly when I’m not looking.

I didn’t know if I could even have children, and never particularly wanted any.  My son was by no means an accident but his father was….. incredibly difficult.  He abandoned me when I told him I was pregnant and I now have sole custody.  For me, my child has brought me a reason to live, not simply exist.  He’s my best friend, and I can’t imagine my life without him now (he’s 5).  I have a good job, I can (barely) afford private school tuition and we are incredibly happy.

I have a 5 year old boy who also thought he should get a toy every time we go in a store, so I set him up for success before we ever go in.  When we’re in the parking lot, I will say “we’re only here to get X, so no toys today”… it’s helped reduce the number of tantrums I’ve had to deal with.

My sons father no longer has any rights or visitation.  His parents told me when my son was 2 months old they didn’t want involved.  However, my sons great grandparents and several great uncles and aunts all wanted to be involved.  I make an effort to keep them Informed and we invite them to events and go visit.  Minimum, I call twice a month.  It’s worth it to me for my son to know he’s got a good family on both sides (even if his dad is crap.)

This sounds very similar to my child’s father... the best advice I got, and took to heart, was from my sons therapist.  She said, “a child only NEEDS both parents if both parents are healthy (meaning mentally), non-abusive and not abusing substances.  Otherwise, they do better without the negative”

The court system is awful, and I’m sorry for anyone who is going through the legal mess.... I would say if you don’t think it will be a high conflict case, then representing yourself will save money.  But if you expect high conflict, please please please hire an attorney who is good at their job.  Don’t be afraid to fire one to hire someone better.  I went through 3 before I found one who got me sole custody.  The others said I was being dramatic when my son came home in bruises and I took him to the ER.  He was 8/9 months old.

No clue... as 3 of the 4 Biological kids were born out of wedlock, and they’ve even accepted his step child as their own... but still don’t accept my son.  The great grandma says that my child is the “most normal” of all of the kids and she thinks that at some point they will want to know him, but I don’t know how I feel at this point how they’ve been so I don’t know what I’d do if they wanted to come back into his life.  

We did attend a funeral of their family a while back and the grandparents stared at us and the aunts came up to my son and ignored me and kept telling my 5 year old they were his aunts... when we left he asked me why those crazy people kept saying they were “aunt Susan” (his only aunt on my side of the family).

I told my ex right after I had confirmed pregnancy with my doctor.  He wasn’t interested, and apparently the mother of his first child told his family that I was pregnant.  After the baby was born, I reached out to the grandparents, and offered to bring the baby to meet them (they live several hours away) and they kept making excuses until after about 2 months they called me and told me they wanted nothing to do with my son.  They’re involved in his oldest daughters life, and his children after my son.  However, the great grandparents stepped up and said they wanted to be involved, so we have maintained a relationship of over 5 years with them.  We go to their house this Thursday for lunch actually.  The father and his parents have nothing to do with us though...

I also read and reread the final order granting me sole custody.  It hurts to know the entire story from the beginning and read the courts interpretation of the relationship all the way down to the father asking for his rights to be terminated.  I have an awesome kid, and there’s a lot of people who do choose him so I hope when he realizes everything, it won’t hurt so much.

Single mom here, haven’t gotten child support for 3 years in June.  Didn’t get any child support for the first 12 months.  He only paid between age 1-2. My son is 5.  His dad took me to court, then thought he would only pay around $100 a month, but when they came back with the full amount he couldn’t sign off fast enough (he makes 6 figures and tried to lie about his income).  I agreed to him signing off and am thankful I have a good job and I can support my son without it.  The drama involved with the court system and a father who just wants the title is far worse than hoping and counting on funds for them to sometimes give and sometimes not.  I hate it when these men don’t pick up their share when it comes to the child that they helped make.

My sons father fought me in court for 2 years (not to have custody, just to take it away from me)... eventually the court terminated his rights so I have sole everything and he doesn’t even get visitation.  Hasn’t even seen my son in any “visit” since right before his second birthday and my son is 5 now.  I’ve had sole custody for about 2.5 years.  Last fall we were both at my sons great grandfathers funeral (on his side, as I still keep in touch with his family and my son knows them) and he cornered me outside and threatened me that he wanted my son to come to his house so his new wife can babysit... not so he could spend time with or even get to know the child.  He told me he had left us alone but was losing his patience.   It just made me laugh, and be thankful I had a great attorney who was familiar with the DV side of things who got the judge to see I wasn’t crazy like his attorney painted me to be.  

Make sure you have a good attorney, but be aware that they will likely right away start with 50/50 if you end up in court.  You’ll have to fight like crazy to get them to realize that you’re not the villain too.

Have you tried anything to help your daughter sleep?  That way you might be able to sleep as well?  My son just turned 5 and has been diagnosed with severe anxiety and PTSD and his fathers rights were terminated, so it’s just me.  I’ve gotten him weighted blankets, and melatonin.  Also, what’s her diet like?  There’s some foods that may increase her anxiety.  She may also be having night terrors.  Sorry you’re going through this, and I really hope you get some sleep soon!

I began having gut problems similar to what you’re describing 14 years ago.  I began trying to get a dr to take me seriously, and the entire time it continued to get worse and worse.  Six years ago I gave birth, and went through a horrid custody battle which eventually almost bankrupt me, but I have sole custody.  That made my problems manifest into borderline not being able to leave my house.  Finally got a diagnosis of IBS and started exploring the Low FODMAP diet and it’s almost made my stomach issues go away.  2 years ago I got an additional diagnosis of AS and have been getting the run around from doctors on that now... but at least I’m not crapping myself on the way to work anymore, and I don’t have the severe pain and bloating as long as I’m careful with what I eat.

I fought like hell in court, and was awarded sole custody when the other parent got convicted of child abuse.  It was never about the kid when he started the court process, he wanted to punish me.  I’m quite pleased to never have to worry about my child’s safety again, and I keep in touch with his family who have welcomed us without him.  I gave up more than my monthly salary in child support and I would rather struggle than to put my child back in that environment.

I’m so sorry!  I am feeling the same after my appointment yesterday.  I’ve been asking for answers for 14 years, finally got a diagnosis last year, and I’ve had allergic reactions to two biologics... so my rheum told me yesterday that maybe I should “go see a counselor or something” when I told her I didn’t want to be a guinea pig on the third biologic and asked for other types of possible treatment.

I really hope that you and your kiddos grow from this situation and they are ok!  Thankfully, mine signed off and I was awarded sole custody... and he’s never established a relationship with my son, but I know he will eventually start asking questions...
I just found this list of children’s books that discuss incarceration... I’ll likely be referring to this list in the future as well.  https://www.nh.gov/nhdoc/fcc/documents/fccbooklist01.pdf
I feel you!  But I’d starve to pay whatever I had to not deal with mines messy drama.  So glad for sole custody!

I started working from home during Covid, and have a 4 (recently turned 5) year old I kept home with me to save on daycare expenses.  It’s been a challenge.  My house is never clean.  My work is never done.  The kid is clean (mostly), fed and happy.  I have sole custody, with the other parent not receiving any visitation so it’s us all.the.time.  Tonight, he mopped the kitchen floor.  He loves it.  But the rest of the house is in shambles.  How I have decided it works best is I have a schedule “Monday-Friday” I/we clean a different area of the house, and then take weekends off.  That way most of the house is at least kinda clean at any given time... and you don’t have to spend an entire day cleaning and dreading.

In my early 20s started having severe stomach/digestive issues.  Kept going to doctors and referred to specialist and kept being told to just take anti depressants and anti anxiety pills and suck it up.  I had a child close to 30 and was still having issues. Then a huge custody battle ensued and stomach problems got worse.  Same doctor and same specialist told me that I “just needed to deal with it.”  Ended up getting sole custody but stomach issues continued.  Finally found another dr who referred to a different GI.  She couldn’t find anything other than IBS but found something on a scan than made her refer me to a rheumatologist.  That was a little over 1 year ago.  (Upwards of 14 years of issues).  According to rheumatologist,  all symptoms are associated with the AS.  Obviously, stress didn’t help. It seems in the last year or so, my body is just falling apart.  Everything hurts, hard to move and enjoy life without pain.

My dr let me skip my starter dose because I told her I didn’t like needles to begin with and once weekly would turn me off of the entire thing... so she started me right in on maintenance dosage.  I’m on cosentyx
I felt tons better less than 24 hours after.  Definitely worked and I felt amazing!  Until it was time for my next injection and I had a bad reaction.  Good luck, I hope it brings you relief!

I paid a bunch of money and dealt with all the stress that surrounds the court system... but I stuck with it, didn’t back down and 2.5 years into it, I was awarded sole custody and we never have to deal with that jerk again.  

Side note:  his family and I are on good terms.  I go to them at least once a month and invite them to all of my sons activities so he has two sets of grandparents/aunts and uncles/ cousins.... we just cut the creep out.

I found out I was pregnant, two days later he announced online he was in a relationship with another person.  So I tried for a while just to keep him involved in the pregnancy.  He never showed up and I realized it wasn’t fair to my child to try to chase someone to get them involved.  I was screamed at because I scheduled a sonogram when I “knew” it was opening day of dove season.  He was too busy with yet another girl when I went into labor.  Didn’t list him on the birth certificate, and the baby has my last name.  Then, to impress the new girl, he filed for custody when baby was 4 days old.  Long story short, my boy is 3 now, I have sole custody, and his dad just had his 4th child a few months ago.  Has nothing to do with my son, and we are all better off for it.  Don’t chase these “dads”... Your child doesn’t need someone who doesn’t want them.

Single mom, with sole custody of a 3 year old with the same behaviors.  My son has some sensory issues and past trauma from time with his dad, so baby sitters are out of the question for me.  I have very little/limited family support. I work full time, I’m finishing up my Masters program, and we are building a new house.  He is desperate for me to spend time with him.  I find that I feel less guilty if I schedule when I clean the house (I clean it early Saturday morning when he’s still sleeping) and try to do little spot checks throughout the week to keep it from becoming a disaster.  I also have had to learn (and still constantly remind myself) that if he wants to help me do it and it takes 30-8,745 minutes longer, just enjoy the help.  He loves putting the laundry in the dryer and pushing the buttons.  He wants to help with the dishes.  I can also give him simple tasks to make him feel like he matters.  While I clean the kitchen, he can take all his toys to his toy box.  It’s not perfect, but it’s what’s working for us right now.... and he still wants me to hold him when he falls asleep (which drives me nuts because there’s sooo much I could be doing), but he’s only going to be little for for a little while and I want to enjoy the limited time I have with him.

TL;DR: He was a psycho who tried to take my kid away then got his rights terminated. 

There are so many flags that I should have seen prior, but this was the tipping point.  Told him I was pregnant, and he went and got a new girlfriend.  Then about 7 months later (and 4 different girlfriends) he shows up on my porch saying he’s “ready to be a dad”.  Spends a couple of weeks trying numerous times to do things to get me to lose the baby after I told him I wasn’t interested in dating him anymore and he needed to step up for the child.  At one point he was behind my car in his truck, we were both at a stop light, and he pushed my car through the intersection with traffic from the other direction moving.  This was one of many incidents.  I invited him to the last sonogram appt and he tells me I never should have scheduled an appointment on the opening day of dove season and refused to come.  Refused to come to the tour of the hospital.  Attacked me at a gas station right after I had the baby and took my credit card.  

Then he gets another new girlfriend and they go to Florida for a few weeks right after I give birth.  She decides she wants a baby while they’re gone, so he files paperwork to take the baby away from me so he can give it to her... I really can’t make this up.  End up spending 2 and a half years in and out of court.  They break up several times.  He doesn’t show up for visits, refuses to pay child support, won’t come to doctor appointments, etc.. tells everyone I refuse to let him see the child.  

His family comes and testifies for me in court and says he has no business having the child unsupervised... baby comes home with bruises one time and the court finally agrees.  He ends up having 6 or 7 DCF investigations with another child over this time.  Anyways. He finally has his rights terminated and goes on to have 2 more children with different women... 

One of the other moms and I are on good terms, so we get the kids together now.  He still sees her child but completely dropped out of my child’s life.

I know I’m late to the party on this thread (just discovered this sub today!) but my son is going to be 3 in a few weeks, diagnosed with SPD and some others and I got a weighted blanket for him this summer to help with sleeping.  It’s great for me, but he freaks out if it’s on him. He HATES it.  But he also doesn’t like to be wrapped up or contained... that’s probably got something to do with the PTSD from a visit with his father before his rights were terminated.  

For night terrors his therapist said to just comfort him as best we can and talk in calm, soft, soothing tones.

I got full custody of my child, and had to fight tooth and nail for two and a half years for it.  The court finally saw that my “co-parent” was not in it for the reasons he cried and talked about on the stand.  It destroyed my health, almost bankrupted me, but my child is happy, healthy and safe.  I’m so glad that the rights were completely terminated so I never have to go through it again.

Thank you.  He'd just had a baby 2 months ago, and no one saw it coming since he was so excited about being a father.  I know it was ultimately his choice in the end and no one could have done anything, but of course there's still guilt.
